title.narrative: Activity under preparation Strengthening internet freedom and resilience (with global reach)

description.narrative: The Russian regime, alongside other authoritarian governments, is investing substantially into digital censorship and surveillance capabilities in an effort to silence independent reporting as well as pro-democratic and anti-war voices. The EU, in turn, supports both independent pluralistic (online and offline) media and civil society activists for their potential to contribute to democracy, human rights and peace and security world wide. At the same time, such initiatives, including EU media or international media such as Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty and independent media in exile, have relied over the past years on censorship circumvention technologies (such as secure, tailor made open source VPNs) financed predominantly by the US. With censorship on the rise, however, the people living in highly repressive environments have a sharply increased need for circumvention technologies and solutions for secure access to free internet which by far exceeds what can be provided from existing programmes. This puts at risk independent reporting as well as pro-democratic and anti-war voices and increases EU vulnerability to malign actors in the region.
